From one sentence to a whole film

From version 2.746.0 each style says where it runs: in its settings (Settings ▸ Image, Video, or Audio ▸ Music styles) set Runs on to Remote GPU, and its name starts with R_. Local lists only the styles for your computer, Remote only the R_ styles, and Both lists them all - an R_ style renders on RunPod, the others on your computer.

From version 2.749.0 bitGen comes with ready-made remote styles for RunPod's own images - nothing to upload: R_SDXL and R_SDXL img2img (the sdxl image), R_FLUX.1 schnell, R_FLUX.1 dev and R_FLUX.1 dev fp8 (the flux1-schnell, flux1-dev and flux1-dev-fp8 images), R_SD3 Medium (sd3) and R_Z-Image Turbo (z-image-turbo). Each image holds one set of models, so bitGen asks RunPod which image your endpoint runs and lists only its styles (Settings ▸ Remote generation ▸ Your endpoint's image).

From version 2.749.0 the studio comes with remote styles for RunPod's own worker images. Each image holds one set of models, and the styles use only those files and ComfyUI's own nodes - nothing to upload.

From version 2.753.0 the studio's LLM - the screenplay writer, prompt help and picture descriptions - can run on OpenRouter: one API key, hundreds of models, some of them free. Nothing to install and no remote GPU needed. Pictures, videos and songs still render on your computer, and its graphics card no longer has to share room with the LLM.
From version 2.756.0 you can find, create and run RunPod pods without leaving bitGen. A pod is your own GPU machine running ComfyUI; you pay for it by the hour while it runs.

From version 2.757.0 bitGen Studio can render without a good graphics card at all: an online service does the work and charges your account for each picture, video or song. No ComfyUI and no models to download - add the service's API key and its styles appear in the style lists.

No tracking, no cookie for counting and no outside analytics service. To learn where our visitors come from, the server counts page views: each one adds 1 to that day's total for the page, the country and state (looked up from your network address on our own server - the address is then dropped), the site you came from, the kind of device and the language. Your projects, pictures, films, voices and settings stay in folders on your own disk. The models run on your own graphics card. bitGen Studio sends nothing about you anywhere. It goes online only when you ask it to: to download models and node packs, to check GitHub for a new version, to send a bug report, or to use a service you set up yourself (a remote GPU, a Hugging Face token).
Your prompts, reference pictures and results travel to RunPod and back over the internet. Rendering on your own computer keeps them at home.
